repo.text: Create the directory `~/{{dotfilesDir}}` and make it a git repository.
repo.hint: `mkdir`, `cd` and then `git init`. Is git not installed? Install it with the package manager, as in the chapter on git.

pack.text: Pack the settings you already have: copy `~/.bashrc` and `~/.gitconfig` to `~/{{dotfilesDir}}`.
pack.hint: `cp` takes several files at once: `cp ~/.bashrc ~/.gitconfig ~/{{dotfilesDir}}/`. Is `~/.gitconfig` missing? Then you haven't told git who you are yet – do it with `git config --global`.

aliases.text: Write the file `{{aliasFile}}` in the repository, with at least two aliases you find useful.
aliases.hint: One alias per line, e.g. `alias ll='ls -la'`. Write the lines with `echo "…" >> {{aliasFile}}` – double quotes outside, single quotes inside.

first-commit.text: Save the state: make a commit that contains both copies and `{{aliasFile}}`.
first-commit.hint: `git add` and then `git commit -m "…"`. Check with `git status` first, so you know what goes in.

secret.text: The Wi-Fi password is going to live in `~/{{dotfilesDir}}/{{secretFile}}`, but it must never end up in the history. Create the file, make git ignore it and commit what that takes.
secret.hint: Write the file's name in `.gitignore` and commit `.gitignore`. `git status` should no longer show `{{secretFile}}`. Has the file already gone into a commit? Then `git rm --cached` removes it from the repository but not from the disk.

branch.text: Try new aliases on a branch: create the branch `{{aliasBranch}}`, add at least one more alias to `{{aliasFile}}` and commit on the branch.

merge-and-use.text: The aliases work – merge `{{aliasBranch}}` into the main branch. Then load `{{aliasFile}}` into the shell with `source` and run one of your aliases.
merge-and-use.hint: `git switch main` and `git merge {{aliasBranch}}`. Then `source {{aliasFile}}` – and type the name of an alias as if it were a command.
